title: Preference sample catalog and slice guides — rerank onboarding kit
body:
Purpose:
This doc is an onboarding kit for creating production-ready reranking evaluation sets when doing model onboarding or regression checks. It focuses on (1) a compact but diverse sampling catalog for pairwise preference annotation, (2) slice definitions + selection heuristics for targeted regressions, and (3) exact NDCG and aggregation rules we use for cross-model comparisons so results are reproducible across teams.

Scope and intended use:
- Intended audience: applied-ml engineers, annotation leads, SRE for eval infra, and solutions engineers validating model rollouts.
- Input: candidate lists produced by a ranking model (top-K) for a set of user queries or prompts.
- Output: a labeled pairwise manifest (A vs B preferences), per-query NDCG@k scores, slice-level aggregated metrics, sample manifests for future audit.

High-level sampling catalog (why these strata)
We recommend partitioning production traffic into non-overlapping strata; each stratum is sampled independently to ensure coverage across behavior modes. Strata below prioritize coverage, not proportional representation. For onboarding/regression tests we use fixed quotas per stratum (numbers below are default for a ~2k query set):
- Popular queries (head): 200 queries. Select by daily unique users >= 95th percentile. Rationale: ensure high-traffic UX unaffected.
- Long-tail queries (tail): 400 queries. Select by frequency percentile <= 25. Captures brittle behavior.
- Ambiguous intent: 250 queries. Heuristic: high entropy over predicted intent classifiers or many labelers disagreeing historically.
- Multi-turn context: 300 queries. Use session join to extract queries with >=2 previous turns.
- Recency-sensitive (fresh content): 200 queries. Include queries where content age < 7 days or queries with time tokens (e.g., "today", "this week").
- Cold-start (new items/entities): 150 queries. Derived from requests referencing newly-indexed docs or new user profiles.
- Hard negatives and adversarial perturbations: 300 queries. Sampled from failure logs and synthetic paraphrase generators.
- Random baseline sample: 200 queries. Uniform sample from the production corpus; useful for sanity checks and calibration.

Pairwise labeling protocol
- Display: present annotator with Query + two candidate outputs (A/B). Candidates are shuffled; annotator must choose one of: Prefer A, Prefer B, No preference / Tie, Not applicable (e.g., content violated).
- Instructions (short): focus only on relevance to the query and instruction-following. Do not penalize harmless style differences unless the query requested a specific format. Penalize hallucinations, factual errors, or missing steps for procedural queries.
- Preference granularity: binary preference with tie allowed. For ties, annotateors must choose tie when outputs are equivalent in relevance and correctness; ties are used in downstream scoring as 0.5 for each pair (see NDCG tie handling).
- Adjudication: each pair gets 3 independent labels. If unanimous -> accept. If 2 vs 1 -> majority wins. If all three different (rare) or two labelers choose "Not applicable" -> escalate to adjudicator who provides final label and rationale.
- Inter-annotator agreement (target): Fleiss' kappa >= 0.6 for primary strata; lower for adversarial strata is acceptable but should be flagged.

Annotation UI hints
- Show context (previous turns) for multi-turn slices.
- Provide explicit markers for code/text blocks vs natural language answers.
- Provide quick examples and a "why" field for adjudicators to write 1–2 sentence rationale in disputed cases.

Label manifest schema (flattened CSV columns)
We expect the labeled output CSV to have these columns: query_id, query_text, candidate_A_id, candidate_B_id, candidate_A_text, candidate_B_text, annotator_1_choice, annotator_2_choice, annotator_3_choice, adjudicated_choice, slice_tags (semicolon-separated), sampling_stratum, generate_time_iso, model_a_version, model_b_version, k_cutoff. All values are plain strings.

NDCG calculation rules (deterministic)
We derive per-query relevance scores from pairwise comparisons via Bradley-Terry (BT) score ranking inside the candidate set and then compute discounted cumulative gain. Steps: 
1) For each query, for each candidate i compute BT-utility u_i using aggregated pairwise wins (regularization: laplace +1 to avoid zeros).
2) Map utilities to relevance grades g_i in {0,1,2} by percentile cutoffs within that query: bottom 50% -> 0, next 35% -> 1, top 15% -> 2 (these thresholds are tunable per dataset; record in metadata).
3) DCG@k = sum_{i=1..k} (2^{g_i} - 1) / log2(i+1). IDCG@k computed on sorted g_i descending. NDCG@k = DCG/IDCG (if IDCG==0, define NDCG=0).
4) For tied candidate grades (due to ties in pairwise), assign fractional grade equal to average position grade for stable IDCG computation.
Notes: we provide both NDCG@5 and NDCG@10 by default. Also compute mean reciprocal rank (MRR) as a complementary metric.

Aggregation and confidence intervals
- Aggregate per-stratum and global NDCG as simple mean over queries, weighted equally. We produce 95% CI using nonparametric bootstrap with 2000 resamples at the query level. Save bootstrap samples (seeded) to allow reproducibility.
- For A/B model comparisons: report mean delta, two-sided bootstrap p-value, and Cohen's d. Flag deltas below 0.2 NDCG points for careful manual triage if CI crosses zero.

Slice definitions and selection heuristics (operational)
We define slices to quickly triage regressions: each slice should map to a modelable predicate on query/candidate metadata. Example slices below with simple selection pseudo-queries.
- "Code-heavy queries": queries containing code tokens (regex: <code> like patterns) OR candidate containing 3+ code blocks.
- "Entity-rich (named-entities)": queries with >2 detected named-entities.
- "Ambiguous intent": top intent-classifier entropy quartile.
- "Multi-turn long context": session_length >= 4 or context_tokens > 512.
- "Length mismatch": query_len_tokens < 8 and candidate_len_tokens > 200 (tests verbosity handling).
- "Recently-changed index": candidate_source_age_days < 14 and candidate_source_change_log != null.

Operational QC and checks before sign-off
- Sanity: run compare-binary to ensure candidate pairs were generated by expected model versions.
- Completeness: ensure at least 95% of sample rows have 3 labels; if less, pause release.
- Agreement heatmap: create per-stratum pairwise agreement heatmap; flag strata with Fleiss' kappa < 0.5.
- Per-annotator bias: measure pref rate per annotator; if any annotator's pref rate > mean +/- 2 std dev -> audit their annotations and retrain.
- Adjudication latency: median adjudication turnaround < 48 hours for critical slices.

Examples (short)
Query: "How to reset my router 2026 model X7"
Candidate A: step-by-step with exact button labels (correct)
Candidate B: general troubleshooting with wrong port names (incorrect)
Expected label: Prefer A.

Query: "Write a haiku about spring rain"
Candidate A: a haiku following 5-7-5 but awkward wording
Candidate B: free-form short poem that is not a haiku
Expected label: Prefer A (format adherence).

Regression investigation workflow (quick)
1) Detect delta on global NDCG or slice NDCG > 0.5 points or p-value < 0.05.
2) Recompute per-query deltas and surface top 50 queries with largest negative delta.
3) Triage by slice and error class (hallucination, truncation, formatting).
4) If systemic, file JIRA with reproduction manifest + candidate examples + minimal reproducer.

Outputs and artifacts to store with each run
- labeled_manifest.csv (schema above)
- bt_utilities.jsonl (one line per query, list of u_i values serialized as string)
- ndcg_report.csv (query_id, ndcg5, ndcg10, mrr, slice_tags)
- bootstrap_samples.tar.gz (seeded sample indices), and a small notes.txt recording thresholds used.

Checklist before merging eval to master
- [ ] Sampling seed recorded and stored.
- [ ] Annotation batch >= 90% complete and Fleiss' kappa computed.
- [ ] Adjudicator notes attached for disputed pairs.
- [ ] CI artifacts uploaded to s3 and links added to run metadata.
- [ ] Evaluation run linked to PR and jira (if rollback risk > threshold).

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide fixed percentile cutoffs for BT->grade mapping across all customers vs per-workload tuning.
- Investigate alternative relevance mapping using ordinal logistic regression instead of hard cutoffs.
- Add automated tooling to detect annotator style drift via embeddings of explanation text.

Contact and ownership
Lead: Ayesha Patel (ap@redwood.ai). Annotation lead: Marco Ruiz. QC owner: Lina Chen. For infra questions contact SRE runbook: JIRA-OPS-1299.

Appendix: reproducibility notes
- Always seed bootstrap RNG with run_id.
- Persist sampling query ids with timestamps and model-version tags.
- Archive adjudication records for 18 months for audit.
